title: RigidBody2D with CCD Ray Cast loses momentum on collision
body:
### Tested versions

v4.5.1.stable.official [f62fdbde1], v4.6.1.stable.official [14d19694e]

### System information

Godot v4.6.1.stable - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - Intel(R) UHD Graphics (Intel Corporation; 31.0.101.2137) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-10510U CPU @ 1.80GHz (8 threads) - 15.75 GiB memory

### Issue description

RigidBody2D fails to transfer full momentum to another RigidBody2D upon collision when Continuous CD is set to Cast Ray. This issue is not noticeable at all speeds or distances between objects, but in some cases the impulse is reduced by several times. 
This is very critical for games like billiards or golf.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/61401d85-bd30-4e5c-b9eb-8d3f6c68c38f

### Steps to reproduce

- Create a 2D scene and add two RigidBody2D nodes, each with a CollisionShape2D (set to CircleShape2D, default radius 10px)
- Align both bodies on the same Y-axis and set their X-axis distance to 21 pixels (leaving a 1-pixel gap between their boundaries)
- Set Gravity Scale to 0 for both bodies
- (Optional) Assign a physics material to both bodies with Bounce set to 1.0
- Set Linear Velocity on the X-axis to 500 (or -500) for one of the bodies (works for 60 physics ticks/sec, e.g. for 120 it works at 1000 px/s)
- Duplicate the pair, on the moving body of the second pair, set Continuous CD to Cast Ray
- Enable "Visible Collision Shapes" in the Debug menu or add sprites to the bodies to visualize the movement
- Run the project and compare the velocities of the target bodies after collision in both pairs

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

This project contains the exact setup described in the "Steps to reproduce" section for immediate testing.

[ccdRcBug.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26059216/ccdRcBug.zip)
